identity.title: Normalize imported external evidence before projection

human_pressure.one_screen_brief: Fix the evidence-to-projection gap proven by second-producer conformance and dogfood: imported package events are stored as EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE wrappers, while projection expects canonical event types such as run_started, project_validation and authority_evidence. Add the smallest normalization boundary so stored raw evidence remains unchanged but production projection observes the wrapped canonical event semantics.
human_pressure.why_now: Without this fix, real package ingestion can succeed while lifecycle, authority, signals and governed outcome remain unknown, preventing meaningful end-to-end dogfood.
do_not_misread: Do not change the persisted EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE storage representation unless repository evidence proves that is required.
Do not add producer-specific EverRun branches.
Do not reinterpret unknown evidence as clean.
red_lines: No producer-identity branching in core governance modules.
No schema rewrite or new ingestion transport.
Do not weaken conflict or idempotency behavior.

machine_core.goal: Make build/rebuild projection consume the canonical event semantics embedded in EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE wrappers while preserving the stored raw event and existing ingestion safety semantics.
red_lines: No raw evidence mutation or evidence loss.
No ingestion idempotency or conflict-check weakening.
Do not introduce a new BLOCKED or HUMAN_REVIEW path for non-capability reasons.
invariants: A non-wrapped native RuntimeEvent continues to project exactly as before.
A well-formed EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE event projects using its embedded original event_type, payload and metadata.
Malformed or incomplete external wrappers remain unknown/safely unprojectable rather than being fabricated.
EverRun and second-producer packages traverse the same normalization path.

observable_effect.assertion: An imported evidence package rebuilds to the same lifecycle and governance facts represented by its canonical embedded events rather than collapsing to unknown solely because storage uses EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE.

proofs.assertion: Existing evidence-package and second-producer tests prove load -> ingest -> rebuild -> projection behavior for wrapped events.

failure_semantics: Malformed EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE payloads do not crash projection and do not become synthetic clean events.
Idempotent re-import and event conflict behavior remain unchanged.

steps.title: Add projection-boundary normalization
details: Detect RuntimeEventType.EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE representation at the projection input boundary.
Expose the embedded original event_type, payload and metadata to projection logic without mutating stored events.

steps.title: Preserve malformed-wrapper safety
details: Handle missing or non-object embedded payloads deterministically.
Never infer a canonical governance event when required wrapper fields are absent.

steps.title: Prove both producer paths
details: Extend existing conformance coverage so an EverRun-style evidence package and the generic second producer both project lifecycle/governance semantics after ingestion.
Keep the anti-regression guard against producer identity branching.

steps.title: Update known limitation
details: Remove or revise the documented EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE projection limitation only after tests prove the production path is fixed.

acceptance: Imported package run_started/run_completed events produce non-unknown lifecycle after rebuild.
Imported authority_evidence can produce AuthorityRecord and corresponding governance signals after rebuild.
Native non-wrapped projection behavior is unchanged.
EverRun-style and second-producer packages share the same projection path with no producer-specific branches.
Ingestion idempotency and conflict behavior remain unchanged.

must_check: Dependency is satisfied: 8047.dogfood-everrun-history-baseline identified or confirmed the projection gap from real dogfood evidence.
The fix occurs at a narrow normalization/projection boundary rather than by rewriting persisted evidence.
Both producer paths traverse identical core governance logic.
Malformed wrappers remain safe and unknown rather than fabricated.
reject_if: The implementation branches on source == everrun or another producer identity in core governance code.
Stored raw evidence is rewritten or flattened destructively.
Idempotency or conflict detection is weakened.
Unknown malformed evidence is treated as valid clean evidence.
A new BLOCKED or HUMAN_REVIEW path is introduced for non-capability reasons.

validation_notes.targeted_contract_coverage: Uses existing second-producer conformance and evidence-package ingestion tests, then full suite for cross-module projection safety.
